Figure 3 shows the cyclic oxidation
mass change data for alloys 230 and 617
up to 2337 cycles. Under these conditions,
dloy 6 17 had lower mass loss compared

Alloys HX, 230 and 188 had substantial
mass gains compared to alloy 617 in this
severe carburization test involving
reducing conditions with no oxygen.

Again alloy 617 showed the
least amount of mass gain compared to the
other three alloys in the second
carburization environment containing a
small partial pressure of oxygen.

The results show that alloys
214 and 230 have poor resistance to the
sulfur containing environment used in this
study compared to alloys 188, 617 and
HX.

The formation of a stable surface
oxide has been shown to be key to
providing resistance to carburization (1-
4).

This retards ingress of carbon into
the alloy.

An
addition of 1 %Al to a Ni-25%Cr alloy has
been shown to improve the adhesion of
scale to the base metal by the formation of
pegs of oxide extending into base metal
(7).

It has also
been shown that the oxide particles of
reactive elements act as vacancy sinks
which otherwise would condense at the
scale metal interface resulting in voids (9-
10).

Alloy
617 is a solid solution strengthened nickel
base superalloy that derives its solid
solution strengthening from substantial
amounts of carbon, cobalt, molybdenum
and chromium.
